title: Do not resolve content references as filesystem entries
body:
Opening a file diff from a remote agent session fails:

```
Unable to read file 'vscode-agent-host://.../changeset/turncontent/2011679d…'
  → -32602 invalid params: unsupported scheme `ahp-session`; expected `file`
```

The changes list populates; only opening a diff fails. Local sessions are fine.

## What the protocol says

A `ContentRef` is "a reference to large content stored outside the state tree". It carries its own `sizeHint` and `contentType`, and `resourceRead`'s `uri` is documented as "Content URI from a `ContentRef`".

`resourceResolve` is "the combination of POSIX `stat` and `realpath`" — its result `type` is `file` \| `directory` \| `symlink`.

So a content ref is **read**, never **resolved**. It is not a filesystem entry, so `resourceResolve` has no answer to give, and needs none: the metadata travels with the ref.

## What we do instead

`AHPFileSystemProvider` serves remote content, so the editor's file layer `stat`s before reading. `stat()` and `realpath()` short-circuited content refs with a hardcoded scheme allowlist:

```ts
if (decoded.scheme === 'session-db' || decoded.scheme === 'git-blob') {
```

Those are two of the shapes VS Code's own host emits, which is why local sessions always hit the shortcut and this went unnoticed. But the shape is the host's choice, and there are already more of them in tree — `agenthost-content:` and `pending-edit-content:` are content refs too, and neither is in the list.

A remote host publishes `ahp-session:/<id>/changeset/turncontent/<sha>`. Not in the list, so the `stat` went to the host, reached its filesystem resolver, and was rejected as a malformed file path. The read that follows would have succeeded — the host routes `/changeset/turncontent/` correctly — but it is never reached.

## Content URI shapes, for comparison

VS Code's own host — path is the real file path, lookup keys in the query:

```
session-db:/Users/me/.copilot/session-state/e580756b/files/capture_addon.py
           ?{"sessionUri":"copilotcli:/9b08d9c3…","toolCallId":"toolu_019SSYR2…"}

git-blob:/Users/me/…/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts
         ?{"sessionUri":"copilotcli:/9b08d9c3…","sha":"3d079185299158cc…"}
```

A remote host — an opaque reference, the path is not a file path:

```
ahp-session:/ab456a26-9bfd-4e69-8538-787d4e664c52/changeset/turncontent/2011679d9182…
```

The protocol's own `resourceRead` example is the same shape as the latter: `ahp-session:/<uuid>/content/img-1`.

## The fix

Stop inferring from the scheme. Callers read these URIs straight out of a `ContentRef` field, so they know what they are holding — that fact was simply dropped when the URI was wrapped for transport, leaving the provider to reconstruct it by sniffing.

`toAgentHostContentUri()` records it in the metadata the transport URI already carries (`?_ah=…`), and `stat` / `realpath` short-circuit on that marker. Because the marker lives in the URI, it survives persistence.

Every site that wraps a `ContentRef` now uses it: the changes view (`agentHostDiffs`, `agentHostSessionFiles`), the chat response file changes, the snapshot controller, and the pending-edit confirmations. The `_diffUriMapper` hook gained an options argument so the two mapper-based sites can signal it.

The scheme allowlist stays, narrowed to its real job: content refs minted before the marker existed, e.g. ones persisted in restored editor state.

## Risk

A wrapped URI without the marker behaves exactly as before. `file:` content refs on the local connection stay unwrapped and resolve normally, as they do today. The only behaviour change is for URIs that previously failed to `stat`.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run valid-layers-check`, `eslint` on all changed files
- `./scripts/test.sh --glob "**/vs/{sessions,workbench/contrib/chat,platform/agentHost}/**/*.test.js"` — 14,620 passing
- New tests: marker round-trip, `stat` and `realpath` not calling the host for a content ref, and `readFile` still reaching it
- One existing snapshot updated — `pending-edit-content:` is a content ref, so its expectation now uses the content wrapper

Control-tested by reverting the marker check: `stat` then reports `resolved: 1` instead of `resolved: 0`, reproducing the production failure rather than merely failing.

title: Never list external Copilot CLI sessions
body:
Follow-up fix for #332547.

That PR removed the `github.copilot.chat.cli.showExternalSessions` setting **and** the origin check it guarded. The intent was for the Copilot CLI provider to *never* list external sessions, but deleting the check inverted it — the provider now *always* lists them.

## Change

`shouldShowSession()` in `copilotcliSessionService.ts` now unconditionally rejects any session whose `IChatSessionMetadataStore` origin isn't `vscode` (e.g. sessions started from the terminal CLI). The check sits right after the untitled-session early return, i.e. *before* the empty-workspace / Agents-workspace escape hatches, so external sessions are filtered regardless of workspace state.

Both listing paths (`getAllSessions` and `constructSessionItemImpl`) funnel through this method. The Agent Host is unaffected — it has its own external-session catalog governed by `chat.agentSessions.showExternalAgentSessions`, which remains authoritative.

## Files

- `copilotcliSessionService.ts` — restore the origin filter, now unconditional
- `copilotCliSessionService.spec.ts` — regression test; verified it fails on the pre-fix code (returns `["external-cli", "vscode-created"]`) and passes now
- `mockChatSessionMetadataStore.ts` — test helper to seed a session origin, since the interface's `setSessionOrigin` only ever writes `vscode`
- `AGENTS.md` — document the now-hardcoded behavior under Critical Pitfalls so it isn't dropped again

## Validation

Full `src/extension/chatSessions` vitest suite passes (1220 tests), no type errors in the touched files.

title: Add copy link actions to the pull request and issue chat pills
body:
The PR/issue chat pills offered no way to copy a reference's link — neither from the single-reference hover nor from the dropdown shown when a session has multiple PRs or issues.

## Description

**Single reference hover**
- `OpenPullRequestActionViewItem` / `OpenIssueActionViewItem` override `getHoverOptions()` to contribute a **Copy Link** status bar action to the rich hover.

**Multi reference dropdown**
- `GitHubReferenceList` entries gained `toolbarActions`, rendered per row in an `ActionBar`; the PR and issue pickers attach a copy action to each entry.
- Row actions re-render only when their presentation key changes, so a focused action survives PR polling updates, and rendered actions delegate to the row's *current* entry rather than the one they were built from.
- The list is now a `Disposable` (it owns the row action bars) and the pickers hold it in a `MutableDisposable`; `createGitHubReferenceListElement` is removed in favour of constructing the list directly.

**References / artifacts chat pill**
- `sessionArtifacts.ts` attaches *Copy Pull Request Link* / *Copy Issue Link* to PR and issue entries, which `ChatDropdownPillActionViewItem` renders in each row's action bar.

**Commands**
- `CopyPullRequestUrlAction` now accepts a `PullRequestActionContext` so it can copy a specific PR; new `CopyIssueUrlAction` mirrors it for issues.

## Supporting fixes

- `HoverService.setupManagedHover`'s `update()` replaced the content but not the options, so a managed hover kept rendering the actions it was created with. Since `BaseActionViewItem.updateTooltip()` always passes fresh options, the pill's copy action would otherwise never appear for asynchronously resolved references, or go stale when the reference changes. Options are now persisted for the next show; the only other option-passing caller (status bar item) also always passes current options, so it gets the same fix.
- Row actions stay visible instead of being revealed on hover: `HoverWidget.findLastFocusableChild` picks the focus-trap wrap target by `tabIndex` regardless of visibility, so a hidden trailing action breaks Shift+Tab inside the dropdown.

## Notes for reviewers

Component fixtures `openPullRequest` and `openIssue` render the pill, hover and dropdown with sample copy actions. New unit tests cover hover option updates (`hoverService.test.ts`), row action rendering and focus retention (`githubContribution.test.ts`), and artifact entry actions (`sessionArtifacts.test.ts`).

title: Flag Agent Merge initiated turns in agent host turn telemetry
body:
## Description

Agent Merge starts turns by sending a host-generated prompt, which was indistinguishable in telemetry from any other host notification. This extends the existing message-origin field with a third value so automated merge work is separable from turns a person or an agent asked for.

**Telemetry**
- `messageOriginKind` on `agentHost.userMessageSent` gains `agentMerge`, alongside the protocol's `user` / `agent` / `tool` / `automation` / `systemNotification`.
- `agentHost.turnCompleted` now reports `messageOriginKind`, so a finished turn is attributable to whoever started it. `turnFailed` / `turnHung` are untouched — `turnCompleted` is emitted for failures too.
- `MessageKind` lives in the auto-generated protocol (`DO NOT EDIT`), so this is a telemetry-only widening: `MessageKind | 'agentMerge'`.

**Identifying merge turns**
- Agent Merge prompts carry `MessageKind.SystemNotification`, but so do the merge notice and Copilot session notifications, so origin kind alone is insufficient. `common/meta/agentMergeMessageMeta.ts` stamps a `vscode.chat.agentMerge` marker into `_meta`, following the `agentMessageDelegationMeta.ts` convention.
- `agentService._startAgentMergePrompt` — the only path that turns a merge decision into a turn — stamps it.
- `getMessageOriginTelemetryKind` honours the marker only on the host-stamped `systemNotification` origin, so a client-supplied `_meta` can't dress a user message up as merge work:

```ts
export function getMessageOriginTelemetryKind(message: Message): AgentHostMessageOriginTelemetryKind {
	if (message.origin.kind === MessageKind.SystemNotification && isAgentMergeMessage(message)) {
		return 'agentMerge';
	}
	return message.origin.kind;
}
```

**Plumbing**
- Threaded through `AgentHostTurnTracker.turnStarted` → `ITurnTiming` → the `turnCompleted` report.
- Queue-drained turns derive it from their message like direct turns.
- Subagent turn starts synthesize a seed message claiming `user` origin; those two call sites now report `tool` explicitly (the protocol's meaning for a tool spawning a worker chat) without altering the stored message.

**Tests**
- Reporter: `agent` / `agentMerge` / `user` on both standard and GitHub events, plus a spoofed-marker user message still reporting `user`.
- End-to-end through `AgentSideEffects`: `turnCompleted.messageOriginKind` is `user` for a user turn and `agentMerge` for a merge turn.

Fixes #332770

Part of #331567

This closes one concrete orchestration gap with the GitHub Copilot App: stacked sessions can now choose the branch they build on. `create_session` accepts an optional `baseBranch`; when provided, Agent Host uses its existing host-owned worktree isolation and branch configuration to create the child session from that branch.

The source chat's provider-owned configuration is preserved when the child uses the same provider. When the model switches providers, only the host-owned worktree settings cross the boundary, so permissions and other provider-specific values do not leak.

The broader gap analysis also found that configured-project discovery, whole-session forking, plan approval, and PR/issue session entry points still require separate host/client seams and are intentionally left for follow-up work.

title: agentHost: run Codex workspace hooks
body:
Fixes #331285

## Problem

A `.codex/hooks.json` hook in the workspace never ran. It showed up correctly in the Customizations view (**Hooks: 1**), but nothing executed.

Codex refuses to *dispatch* a hook until its exact command hash has been recorded as trusted in `config.toml`. That ledger is only written by the codex TUI's startup hook-review screen — a surface agent host users never reach — so workspace hooks were discovered and then silently dropped.

Confirmed by driving `codex app-server` directly, outside VS Code:

| run | `hooks/list` | hook ran |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | `sessionStart` / `untrusted` | ❌ |
| `bypass_hook_trust: true` | `sessionStart` / `untrusted` | ✅ |

Project trust was a red herring: `thread/start` already auto-persists `projects.<cwd>.trust_level = "trusted"` on its own, and the hook still did not run.

## Change

Pass `bypass_hook_trust` on every codex thread via a shared `codexThreadBaseConfig` fragment, applied to all four thread-creation paths — `thread/start` (materialize + side chat), `thread/fork`, and `thread/resume`.

This is the documented purpose of the flag ("automation that already vets hook sources"). The agent host vets them up front: `_ensureFoldersTrusted` refuses to start a session until **every** working directory passes VS Code Workspace Trust. That makes codex's per-hook ledger redundant here, and brings Codex in line with the Claude and Copilot harnesses, which already run workspace hooks.

Enterprise policy is unaffected: `HookDiscoveryPolicy::allows` is independent of `bypass_hook_trust`, so `allow_managed_hooks_only` still wins. Verified both by reading the codex source and empirically. Per the `policy-and-managed-settings` guidance this control stays runtime-owned, so no VS Code policy is added.

**Coupled fix:** `ALWAYS_CHECKED_EDIT_PATTERNS` covered `.github/hooks/**` and `.claude/settings*.json` but not `.codex`. Since these hooks now actually execute, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.codex/config.toml` and `.codex/agents/**` are added so the agent cannot silently install one without user confirmation.

## Validation

Built Code OSS and ran a real A/B in the Agents window, same build / workspace / prompt, using the issue's exact `hooks.json`:

- **With the fix** — `.codex-dummy-hook.log` created; agent host logged `hook/started` + `hook/completed`
- **Fix reverted** — no log, no `hook/*` notifications (bug reproduced)

`npm run compile` and `npm run hygiene` are clean. `CodexLaunchConfig` 4/4 and the lifecycle-hook / casing permission tests pass.

title: fix: guard against cleared view model in ChatWidget._acceptInput (fixes #332754)
body:
### Summary

`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'model')` is thrown from `ChatWidget._acceptInput` when the chat view model is torn down (session switch or model disposal) while a submission is still in flight. The method validates `this.viewModel` once near the top, but then executes several more `await` points before dereferencing `this.viewModel.model`; a concurrent `setModel(undefined)` / `onDidDisposeModel` can null the field in between, so the later unconditional read throws. Impact: benign-looking unhandled error surfaced to telemetry whenever a user submits chat input as the session is being replaced or disposed.

Fixes microsoft/vscode\#332754
Recommended reviewer: `@connor4312`

### Culprit Commit

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Commit | [`798ef5910034`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/798ef5910034) |
| Author | `@connor4312` |
| PR | #277944 |
| Message | chat: remove `waitForReady` (#277944) |
| Why | This commit reworked `_acceptInput` to wait for a view model and added the single early-return guard at the top of the method (`if (!this.viewModel) { return; }`). It did not re-validate `this.viewModel` after the subsequent `await` points (submit handler, `saveAllBeforeChatSend`, slash-command execution, request cancellation, `finishedEditing`), so a concurrent teardown between the guard and the `const model = this.viewModel.model` read can null the field and produce the `TypeError`. |

### Code Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as User
    participant Accept as _acceptInput()
    participant Teardown as setModel(undefined) / onDidDisposeModel
    participant Crash as this.viewModel.model

    User->>Accept: submit input
    Note over Accept: guard: if (!this.viewModel) return  (passes)
    Accept->>Accept: await submitHandler / saveAll / slash cmd / cancel / finishedEditing
    Teardown-->>Accept: this.viewModel = undefined (concurrent session switch/dispose)
    Accept->>Crash: const model = this.viewModel.model
    Note over Crash: 💥 TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'model')
```

### Affected Files

| File | Role | Evidence |
|------|------|----------|
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatWidget.ts` | crash site | L3209 (from stack): `const model = this.viewModel.model;` |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatWidget.ts` | producer | L2640: `this.viewModel = undefined;` in `setModel(undefined)`, and L2721: `this.viewModel = undefined;` in the `onDidDisposeModel` handler |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatWidget.ts` | existing guard pattern | L3100-3102: `if (!this.viewModel) { return; }` and L3165: `const isEditing = this.viewModel?.editing;` |

### Repro Steps

This is a timing-dependent teardown race; it is not deterministic.

1. Open a chat session and type a message.
2. Submit the message (Enter) while simultaneously switching to another chat session or triggering session disposal (e.g. closing/clearing the chat) so that `setModel` runs during the in-flight `_acceptInput` awaits.
3. To increase likelihood, use a custom `submitHandler` or a slow `saveAllBeforeChatSend` (many dirty editors) to widen the await window between the top-of-method guard and the `this.viewModel.model` read, then dispose/replace the model during that window.
4. The unhandled `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'model')` is thrown from `_acceptInput`.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach**: In `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatWidget.ts` → `_acceptInput()`, re-validate `this.viewModel` immediately before the `const model = this.viewModel.model` dereference and bail out (`return`) when it has been cleared. This mirrors the method's own existing patterns: the top-of-method guard at L3100 and the optional access at L3165 (`this.viewModel?.editing`) already acknowledge that the view model can disappear across awaits. The fix stops the in-flight submission when the session it belonged to no longer exists — the correct behavior, since there is no model left to submit to.

This is a lifecycle/race error, so the guard is placed to stop the consumer from acting on state that a concurrent teardown invalidated. The producer (`setModel(undefined)` / `onDidDisposeModel`) legitimately clears `this.viewModel` as part of normal session lifecycle; it cannot avoid nulling the field, and the in-flight `_acceptInput` continuation is the party that must observe the change. Re-reading the field under the same synchronous section as the dereference makes the invalid ordering unrepresentable at the crash site without swallowing any error — no `logService.error` or throw is removed, and the guard fires only for the genuine “session went away mid-submit” case.

**Lifecycle pattern**: stale cached identifier / use-after-clear across await boundaries.
**Producer site**: `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatWidget.ts:2640` and `:2721` — the two paths that set `this.viewModel = undefined` during session switch/dispose.

**Alternatives considered**: Wrapping the dereference in `try/catch` — rejected because it would hide the lifecycle error from telemetry rather than making the invalid ordering explicit. Adding `?.` and continuing — rejected because the rest of the method unconditionally uses `model`/`this.viewModel`, so a null model must abort the submission, not proceed with an undefined value.

### Recommended Owner

`@connor4312` — culprit commit author of #277944 which introduced the `_acceptInput` view-model wait/guard logic; active VS Code team member with write access (recent commits within the last day).

title: sessions: track manually typed characters in session summary telemetry
body:
Adds two fields to the `agents/sessionSummary` telemetry event that report how much the user hand-edited a session's workspace rather than letting the agent do the work:

- **`typedCharacters`** — characters the user manually typed into files inside the session's workspace folders.
- **`typedFileCount`** — how many distinct such files they typed into.

## How it works

A new `SessionsTypedCharactersTracker` observes the text models of the window it runs in and counts only edits that pass the editor's existing `isUserEdit()` predicate, so agent edits, accepted suggestions, paste and undo/redo are all excluded.

The Agents window is a separate renderer with its own `IModelService`, so the "don't capture typing done in a regular window" requirement falls out of the architecture: models from another window never reach this tracker.

Typing fires one content change per keystroke, so counts are buffered per resource and flushed in batches rather than persisting on every key.

## Notes for reviewers

Three decisions worth a look:

- **Attribution is to the active session only.** An earlier revision scanned every known session per flush; that was wasteful, and the user only edits the session they are looking at. Because flushing is batched, the active session is cached and the buffer flushed *before* adopting a new one — otherwise typing in session A followed by a quick switch to B would land on B.
- **Resources are matched against `folder.workingDirectory`, not `folder.root`.** For a worktree session the root is the shared repository checkout, which the session itself never edits, so matching the root would misattribute. The folder check also keeps typing in the chat input box (itself a text model) out of the count.
- **File identity is persisted as a hash, capped at 250 per session.** The lifecycle tracker persists to application storage, so keeping raw URIs would put the user's file paths on disk for the lifetime of every tracked session. Only the count is ever reported.

## Drive-by fix

`folderCount` / `gitFolderCount` / `nonGitFolderCount` / `isMultiRoot` were captured once when a session was first observed and never refreshed, so a session whose workspace resolved asynchronously or gained folders later reported stale counts. They are now refreshed on each interaction (skipping empty/unresolved workspaces, so teardown does not overwrite good values with zeros). Classification comments updated to match.

## Validation

`typecheck-client`, `eslint` and `valid-layers-check` are clean; **180 tests pass** across the full sessions contrib suite. New tests cover the user-edit predicate, per-resource batching, model add/remove, distinct-file counting with cap saturation, working-directory scoping, attribution across a session switch, and last-observed folder counts.

`npm run hygiene` fails in this environment at its first step with a doubled drive letter (`C:\C:\...\remote\package.json`) — reproduced identically on a clean tree, so it is pre-existing and unrelated.

title: Setting to detect and auto-resolve merge conflicts

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

body:
## Problem

The Agents Window monitors CI failures for pull requests associated with sessions. When a pull request has merge conflicts, CI usually does not run, so the existing CI failure notification never appears.

Agent Merge can already resolve conflicts when `chat.agentMerge.resolveConflicts` is enabled, but only for sessions where Agent Merge has also been enabled explicitly. It does not provide global monitoring across all sessions.

## Proposal

Add an opt-in setting that monitors pull requests associated with every eligible session in the Agents Window. When a merge conflict is detected, automatically ask that session agent to resolve the conflict and update the pull request. The request should only be submitted once for the current pull request head so polling cannot start duplicate turns.

This should remain opt-in because it starts agent turns and modifies repository branches without a direct per-session action, which may consume model usage and create unexpected changes if enabled implicitly. This is intentionally broader than the existing per-session Agent Merge consent model.

title: git: don't reveal deleted resources in OS file explorer
body:
Fixes #332749

## Summary

`git.revealFileInOS` (Reveal in File Explorer / Finder / Open Containing Folder) and `git.revealInExplorer` are contributed to the `scm/resourceState/context` menu for every Source Control resource, including resources with `Status.DELETED` / `INDEX_DELETED` / `BOTH_DELETED`.

The menu's `when` clause can only check `scmResourceGroup` / `remoteName` / platform — there's no per-resource-status context key available to hide these entries only for deleted files, so they stay visible and clickable even though the target path no longer exists on disk.

Clicking them currently does nothing observable: the underlying `shell.showItemInFolder` (and the Explorer/Finder reveal command) is a no-op when the path is missing, so the user gets no feedback at all.

## Fix

Guard both commands the same way `git.openFile` already guards against deleted resources (see its existing `.filter(r => r.type !== Status.DELETED && r.type !== Status.INDEX_DELETED)`), and show a warning message instead of failing silently.

`DELETED_BY_US` / `DELETED_BY_THEM` (modify/delete merge conflicts) are intentionally left unaffected — verified that git leaves the "theirs"/"ours" content in the working tree for those, so there is something real to reveal.

## Test plan

- [x] Deleted file (working tree) → warning shown, no reveal attempted
- [x] Modified/existing file → reveals normally, unaffected
- [x] Modify/delete merge conflict (`DELETED_BY_US`) → reveals normally, unaffected
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` passes

Either the menu entry is hidden for deleted resources, or clicking it gives some feedback.

## Actual

The menu entry is shown and clickable, but clicking it does nothing observable — no Explorer/Finder window opens, no error, no message. The command silently no-ops because the underlying `shell.showItemInFolder` does nothing when the target path doesn't exist, and neither `git.revealFileInOS` nor `git.revealInExplorer` (in `extensions/git/src/commands.ts`) check whether the resource still exists before invoking it.

I have a fix ready (guard both commands the same way `git.openFile` already guards against deleted resources, and show a warning instead of failing silently) — will open a PR referencing this issue.

title: Local history: await model resolution before merge window decision
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.

Fixes #332737

`WorkingCopyHistoryModel.addEntry` decided whether to replace the latest entry (merge window) by reading `this.entries.at(-1)` without awaiting model resolution first, unlike every other entry-mutating path (`removeEntry`, `updateEntry`, `getEntries`, `store`). On a freshly constructed model - first save of a file after window start or reload - `entries` is still empty even when `entries.json` on disk holds a same-source entry seconds old, so the merge-window replacement is skipped and a duplicate history entry is created.

The fix awaits resolution at the top of `addEntry`, mirroring `doStore`. Resolution is memoized and only reads from disk, so there is no deadlock and no reordering for already-resolved models; the observable change is confined to fresh models, where add/replace events now fire after the disk read they depend on anyway.

Draft until #332737 receives triage.

## How was this tested

```
node build/next/index.ts transpile
".build/electron/Code - OSS.exe" test/unit/electron/index.js --crash-reporter-directory=.build/crashes --run vs/workbench/services/workingCopy/test/electron-browser/workingCopyHistoryService.test.js
```

A new test reproduces the reload cycle end to end over a shared in-memory file system: save an entry, dispose the service, recreate it (fresh unresolved model), save again within the merge window, and assert one merged entry results. Against the unfixed source it fails with two entries (`2 !== 1`); with this change the suite runs 21 passing, 0 failing, and the adjacent working copy suites pass unchanged (tracker 27, backup service 58, backup tracker 77).

title: Local history: first save after reload duplicates an entry instead of merging within the merge window

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: workbench-history
labels.description: History item issues

body:
### Bug description

`WorkingCopyHistoryModel.addEntry` (`src/vs/workbench/services/workingCopy/common/workingCopyHistoryService.ts`) reads `this.entries.at(-1)` to decide whether the newest entry should be replaced (merge window) without awaiting model resolution first. Every other entry-mutating path (`removeEntry`, `updateEntry`, `getEntries`, `store`) awaits `resolveEntriesOnce()` before touching `this.entries`; a freshly constructed model starts with `entries = []` and resolves lazily.

Consequence: on the first save of a file after session start (or after a window reload), `lastEntry` is undefined even when the on-disk `entries.json` holds a same-source entry seconds old, so `doAddEntry` always runs and a duplicate history entry is created instead of replacing the previous one. The `workbench.localHistory.mergeWindow` setting (default 10s) documents that "the last entry in local history is replaced" for saves within the interval, which this path violates.

Concrete sequence: save `file.txt`, quit within the merge window or let the scheduler flush, reopen the window, save again 5 seconds later - two entries 5 seconds apart with identical source appear where one replaced entry was promised.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable local history for a workspace, save a file.
2. Reload the VS Code window.
3. Save the same file again within `workbench.localHistory.mergeWindow`.
4. Open Timeline (Local History): two entries exist instead of one replaced entry.

### Expected behavior

`addEntry` resolves pending entries from disk first (like its sibling methods), then applies the merge-window replacement logic against the real latest entry.

title: Main process dies with no dialog: STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW (0xC00000FD) — unbounded recursion at Code.exe+0x1979730 on CrBrowserMain
body:
- VS Code Version: **1.134.0**, commit `110a328ea54b42367b803ec53ee0bf52ef26b419`, x64 system install, build date `2026-08-18T18:24:44Z`
- OS Version: **Windows 11 Enterprise 25H2**, build 26200 (10.0.26200)
- WSL: 2.6.1.0, kernel 6.6.87.2-1, Ubuntu 22.04 (some crashes involve a remote window, some do not — see below)
- Reproduces without extensions: **Yes** (`--disable-extensions`, crashed in 55 s)
- crash-reporter-id: **`3f32d9e5-ab94-4c62-bb03-8dd7b3fc2242`** (crash reporter enabled, so the dumps below were uploaded)

## Symptom

VS Code vanishes instantly with **no dialog and no "window crashed" recovery UI**. Every window
dies at once — local and WSL-remote together — because they share the one Windows main process.
Auto-restart does not always happen. **14 occurrences between 2026-08-24 and 2026-08-26.**

## Crash signature — byte-identical in all 14 dumps

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Exception | `0xC00000FD` = `STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW` |
| Crashing thread | **`CrBrowserMain`** (browser/main process, 86–113 threads) |
| Fault address | `Code.exe+0x1976cb5` (once `+0x1976d08`) |
| Repeated return address | **`Code.exe+0x1979730`, ×37,350–37,361** |
| Companion value in each frame | `Code.exe+0xcdad800` (lands in `.rdata`/`.data` — a static object pointer, not a return address) |
| Stack frame stride | 224 bytes |
| Stack captured | 8188 KiB, **100% consumed** |

**This is an unbounded cycle, not deep-but-finite data.** 8 MiB ÷ 224 B = 37,449 maximum frames;
~37,355 observed. The stack is exhausted right to its limit every time, so recursion depth
carries no information about input size — it would look identical with 5 items or 500.

Because the overflow is on `CrBrowserMain`, the "window crashed" handler cannot run, which is why
there is no dialog and why all windows go together.

Collateral child-process dumps are written in the same second every time and can be ignored:
`node.CrUtilityMain` with `0xC0000005` (params `0x0, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`) and `0xE06D7363`
(MSVC C++ exception). They are children dying with the parent.

## Steps to reproduce

I do not have a deterministic repro, and I want to be upfront about that. What I can say:

- The only activity present in **all 14** crashes is an **agentic CLI tool actively working in an
  integrated terminal** — continuously emitting output and updating the terminal. Crashes never
  happened while the editor was idle.
- Uptime at crash ranges **9 s → 2 h 46 min** with no pattern. It has happened seconds after
  launch and hours into a session.

  crash** in every fully-captured case (e.g. last main-process log line 40 min before, 46 min

  precursor line to correlate against.

- **Window/session restore** — crashes at 17.5 min and 2 h 44 min uptime, long past restore

`Code.exe`'s CodeView record names pdb `electron.exe.pdb`, GUID
`C28016007B74C5D84C4C44205044422E`, age 1. The GUID tail `4C4C44205044422E` decodes to ASCII

title: ScopedProgressIndicator stores whileStart and whileDelay swapped in showWhile
body:
### Bug description

`ScopedProgressIndicator.showWhile` (`src/vs/workbench/services/progress/browser/progressIndicator.ts`) constructs its while-state with two arguments swapped:

```ts
new ProgressIndicatorState.While(promise, delay || 0, Date.now())
```

against the constructor signature

```ts
constructor(whilePromise, whileStart, whileDelay)
```

so `whileStart` holds the configured delay and `whileDelay` holds the creation timestamp. Introduced when scoped progress was made generic in early 2022 (commit `3cdf4d82eadb`), line 305 remains the only construction site.

Today this produces no visible misbehavior only because the replay formula happens to be symmetric under the swap: `whileDelay - (Date.now() - whileStart)` evaluates to the same number either way. The damage is latent:

- `whileDelay` is fed to a `> 0` guard as a wall-clock timestamp, so the guard can never be false;
- any future consumer of `whileStart`/`whileDelay` reading them per their names gets wrong values;
- the replay arithmetic silently depends on an accidental algebraic coincidence between the constructor contract and one call site.

### Steps to reproduce

Read line ~305 against the `ProgressIndicatorState.While` constructor at ~129: the second argument is the configured delay, the third is `Date.now()`, reversing the declared parameter order.

### Expected behavior

`whileStart` receives the wall-clock start time and `whileDelay` receives the configured delay, matching the parameter names and every other use of those fields.

### Version tested

Commit `3746c6426bc6` on `main`; verified by executing compiled output and by a new unit assertion pinning the stored fields. A one-line fix plus regression test is ready.

body:

* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Fixes #332730

`WriteableStream.destroy()` cleared `pendingWritePromises` without settling it, so every producer parked inside `await stream.write()` under backpressure stayed parked forever after a destroy. Reachable through the file service copy pipeline: when a consumer stream created with a `highWaterMark` is destroyed mid-transfer, the read loop in `io.ts` never returns from its awaited write and the `finally` that closes the source file handle never runs. The codebase already treats this hang class as a bug elsewhere (`ResourceQueue.dispose` releases its drainers "to prevent hanging promises").

The fix stores pending writes as resolve/reject pairs and has `destroy()` reject them all with an error, mirroring how dispose paths elsewhere release waiters. Writing to an already-destroyed stream kept its existing silent no-op; only the parked-writer hang is addressed.

Draft until #332730 receives triage.

## How was this tested

```
node build/next/index.ts transpile
node node_modules/mocha/bin/mocha.js test/unit/node/index.js --delay --ui=tdd --timeout=5000 --exit --run out/vs/base/test/common/stream.test.js
```

Two tests were added next to the highWaterMark block: destroying a stream with a pending backpressure write now settles that write (the pre-fix run fails this test by timing out on the literal hang), and writing to a destroyed stream keeps returning synchronously instead of queueing. Before the production change: 26 passing, 1 failing; after: 27 passing, 0 failing.

Additional verification performed during development:

- every production caller that creates streams with a highWaterMark was audited (`htmlFileSystemProvider`, `fileImportExport`, `agentHostRequestService`): all wrap their awaited write in try/catch, so the new rejection is handled and previously hung paths now unwind to their cleanup
- streams without a highWaterMark never produce pending write promises, so their destroy behavior is unchanged

title: WriteableStream.destroy leaves producers awaiting backpressure writes hung forever
body:
### Bug description

`WriteableStream.destroy()` (`src/vs/base/common/stream.ts`) clears the pending write queue without settling it:

```ts
this.pendingWritePromises.length = 0;
```

`write()` documents returning a promise the producer must await before writing more (backpressure); those promises are the queued resolvers. After a destroy, every producer parked inside `await stream.write()` stays parked forever, and nothing rejects.

The codebase treats this class of hang as a bug elsewhere: `ResourceQueue.dispose` explicitly releases its drainers "to prevent hanging promises".

Reachable through the file service copy pipeline: `src/vs/platform/files/common/io.ts` awaits `target.write(...)` between chunks with consumer streams created with a `highWaterMark`; if the target stream is destroyed mid-transfer (error or cancellation path), the read loop hangs permanently and the `finally { provider.close(handle) }` never runs, so the source file handle leaks. The token is only checked between iterations, so cancellation cannot unblock the parked write either.

Minimal repro:

1. `newWriteableStream(string, { highWaterMark: 1 })`
2. `stream.write('a')` (accepted), then `const p = stream.write('b')` (returns pending backpressure promise)
3. `stream.destroy()`
4. Observe `p` never settles.

### Expected behavior

Destroying a stream settles pending writes - by error-rejecting them (`onError`) so producers unwind and their cleanup paths run.

title: refactor handling of enabled/disabled state of built-in skills in the Agents window
body:
## Summary

This restores Enable/Disable support for built-in skills in the Agent Host Customizations UI while keeping `PureItemProviderItemSource` a pure projection of provider output.

Enabled built-in skills are synchronized to the Agent Host as user customizations. The Agent Host merges them with the customizations it discovers and publishes the resulting set back to VS Code through its item provider.

Disabled built-in skills require special handling because they are intentionally excluded before synchronization and therefore cannot be returned by the Agent Host. To keep them visible and allow users to re-enable them, the Agent Host item provider supplements its output with locally known disabled built-in skills.

The implementation:

- Restricts user enablement state to built-in skills. Other customization types and storage sources are unaffected.
- Marks user-disabled built-in skills during local customization enumeration.
- Excludes disabled built-in skills before creating the customization bundle sent to the Agent Host.
- Adds missing disabled built-in skills to the item provider output with `enabled: false`, preserving their original URI so the existing Enable action can update the correct prompts-service entry.
- Overrides stale enabled provider rows while synchronization is in progress, avoiding duplicate or temporarily enabled entries.

Fixes #332721

`TernarySearchTree.has` reported true for any strict prefix of a stored key, because its condition accepted nodes that merely have a `mid` chain:

```ts
return !(node?.value === undefined && node?.mid === undefined);
```

so after `set('foobar', 1)` a lookup of `foo`, `fo` or `f` returned true while `get` returned undefined for the same keys. The separate `hasElementOrSubtree` method exists precisely for subtree-existence semantics; exact-key membership is what `has` was meant to provide. The fix makes `has(key)` agree with `get(key) !== undefined`.

Reachable effects of the loose form: the context key service takes a `has` shortcut before falling back to settings, so asking for `config.editor` after only `config.editor.fontSize` was cached yielded undefined instead of the composed value; and the parcel file watcher treated a request path that is a prefix of an already-watched path as already watched, adding a redundant recursive watcher.

Draft until #332721 receives triage.

```
node build/next/index.ts transpile
node test/unit/node/index.js --run out/vs/base/test/common/ternarySearchtree.test.js
```

A new test pins prefix lookups (`has('foobar')` true, `has('foo')`/`has('f')`/`has('x')` false, `get('foo')` undefined) plus a falsy-value case (`set('bar', 0)`, `has('bar')` true). Against the unfixed source the prefix assertions fail; with this change: 33 passing, 0 failing.

- randomized shared-prefix trials with delete/deleteSuperstr interleaved: new implementation agrees with `get() !== undefined` on every probe (~24k), while the old one diverged on ~42% of probes

title: TernarySearchTree.has reports true for strict prefixes of stored keys
body:
### Bug description

`TernarySearchTree.has` (`src/vs/base/common/ternarySearchTree.ts`) returns:

```ts
return !(node?.value === undefined && node?.mid === undefined);
```

A key that is a strict prefix of a stored key lands on an intermediate node with `value === undefined` but `mid !== undefined`, and `has` reports true even though `get` returns undefined for that key. The separate `hasElementOrSubtree` method exists precisely for subtree-existence semantics, so exact-key membership is what `has` was meant to provide.

Minimal repro with a forStrings trie: `set('foobar', 1)` then `has('foo') === true`, `has('f') === true`, while `get('foo') === undefined`.

### Steps to reproduce

Two reachable effects:

1. `contextKeyService.ts` uses the trie for cached `config.*` context values and takes a `has` shortcut before falling back to the settings object: asking for `config.editor` after only `config.editor.fontSize` was cached yields `undefined` instead of the composed settings value.
2. `parcelWatcher.ts` classifies a request path as already watched when it is merely a prefix of another stored watch path, adding a redundant recursive watcher (request `/a/b` while `/a` and `/a/b/c` are stored).

### Expected behavior

`has(key)` agrees with `get(key) !== undefined`: only stored keys count.

Fixes #332715

`TernarySearchTree.deleteSuperstr` cleared all three child links of the prefix node, but only the `mid` chain holds superstrings; `left` and `right` hold unrelated keys that merely sort around that character position. Deleting a prefix therefore wiped unrelated entries: with config-shaped keys, deleting superstrings of `config.editor` emptied a trie that also held `config.files.autoSave`. The context key service calls this on every non-default-source settings change, so unrelated cached context values vanished and stayed missing from `collectAllValues()` until something recomputed them.

Three coordinated corrections in `_delete`, all serving that one semantics:

- the superstring branch clears only `node.mid`;
- with left/right surviving, the value-less prefix node can now reach the BST removal path whose successor copy previously orphaned the successor's own equal-child chain; that chain moves up together with the copied segment (this also fixes the same loss in plain `delete()`, reproducible today with keys `ab, aa, ac, acd`);
- the removal guard no longer treats stored falsy values as absent, so an exact key holding `0`, `false` or `''` survives deleting its superstrings.

Draft until #332715 receives triage.

## How was this tested

```
node build/next/index.ts transpile
node test/unit/node/index.js --run out/vs/base/test/common/ternarySearchtree.test.js
```

Two new tests pin sibling survival for strings and for config-key segments (including the both-side-sibling shape that reaches the successor-copy path), one pins falsy exact-key retention, and one existing expectation in the config delete_superstr test was corrected: it previously required `config.boo` to vanish even though that key does not extend the deleted prefix - it could only pass because of the bug. Before the change the suite measures 33 passing with 2 failing new assertions; after it, 35 passing, 0 failing.

Additional verification performed during development:

- randomized old-vs-new differential across all four iterator factories (strings, paths, config keys, uris) against a reference model enforcing "remove keys strictly extending the prefix, keep the exact key": zero divergences for the new code over ~120k operations, balance asserted after every operation
- AVL bookkeeping verified unaffected: height derives from left/right only, `mid` never contributes

title: TernarySearchTree.deleteSuperstr deletes unrelated sibling keys
body:
### Bug description

`TernarySearchTree.deleteSuperstr` (`src/vs/base/common/ternarySearchTree.ts`) clears all three child links when it finds the node holding the prefix:

```ts
if (superStr) {
    // removing children, reset height
    node.left = undefined;
    node.mid = undefined;
    node.right = undefined;
```

Only the `mid` chain holds superstrings (keys extending the prefix). `left` and `right` hold unrelated keys that merely sort around that character position, so wiping them deletes entries that are not superstrings of the deleted prefix at all. The repo's own tests already pin the intended semantics elsewhere (`deleteSuperstr('/user/fo')` must be a no-op for `/user/foo`, and sibling survival is asserted in other scenarios), but no test covers a sibling sitting at the terminal node.

Minimal repro with a forStrings trie:

1. `set('d', 1); set('e', 2);`
2. `deleteSuperstr('d')`
3. The trie now holds only `d`; `e` is gone.

With config-shaped keys: after `set('config.editor.fontSize')`, `set('config.editor.formatOnSave')`, `set('config.files.autoSave')`, calling `deleteSuperstr('config.editor')` empties the whole trie instead of keeping `config.files.autoSave`.

### Steps to reproduce

Run the three-line script above against any build, or observe context key values: the sole production caller (`contextKeyService.ts`) calls `deleteSuperstr` on the cached `config.*` trie whenever non-default-source settings change, which drops unrelated cached values, omits them from the fired change event's key list, and leaves them missing from `collectAllValues()` until something recomputes them.

### Expected behavior

Only the `mid` subtree is removed; `left` and `right` siblings stay intact.

title: perf: keep session lookups out of per-file agent feedback loops
body:
Narrow fix for the feedback/annotations part of #332670.

Switching sessions could block the renderer for seconds. The agent feedback overlay iterates every original/modified URI of the active multi-diff and did **session-scoped** work per file: `getFeedbackSessionResource()` -> `getFeedback()` -> `getSessionEditorComments()`. Every one of those ends up calling `ISessionsManagementService.getSession()`, which rebuilds each provider's session catalog and then scans it linearly. With a 6,600-file Changes editor that is ~13k catalog rebuilds; a session with *no* feedback is the worst case because nothing stops the scan early.

### Changes

- `AgentFeedbackService._resolveSession()`: resolve through the active `IActiveSession` facade when the requested resource is the active session, and otherwise from a single-entry memo of the last lookup (hit **or** miss). The memo is dropped on `onDidChangeSessions` and when the session is deleted, so it never outlives a catalog change. Used by `getSessionForFile()`, `_isAgentHostSession()` and `_sessionContainsResource()` - the last two run on every `getFeedback()` call.
- `getFeedbackSessionCandidates()`: lazily maps resource candidates to their feedback session and yields each distinct session at most once, so feedback/backend work runs once per session instead of once per file. Used by the editor overlay and the feedback editor actions; both keep their early exit once a session with comments is found.
- `getSessionForFile()` now checks file eligibility before resolving anything (same result, no lookup for ineligible resources).

### Tests

New unit tests cover the dedupe over a 4,000-candidate multi-diff (including that iteration stops resolving once the caller breaks) and the session resolution: active session needs no management-service lookup, a non-active session is looked up once until sessions change, and an unknown session is remembered as unknown.

Not addressed here (separate areas from the issue): the archived worktree lifecycle and the `getSession()` lookup contract itself.

title: Agent Host: clean-env agent spawn on Windows strips APPDATA/ProgramFiles/ComSpec etc., breaking dotnet/NuGet and gh in agent sessions
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

- VS Code Version: 1.134.0 (commit 110a328ea54b42367b803ec53ee0bf52ef26b419, stable, x64)
- OS Version: Windows 11 Education N 10.0.26200
- Agent: Claude via Agents window (Claude Agent SDK 0.3.220 / claude-code 2.1.220)

## Summary

On Windows, shell commands executed by an agent session (Claude, Agents window) run in an environment that is missing core Windows environment variables: `APPDATA`, `LOCALAPPDATA`, `ProgramData`, `ProgramFiles`, `ProgramFiles(x86)`, `ComSpec`, `PATHEXT`, `NUMBER_OF_PROCESSORS`, `PROCESSOR_*`, `OS`, `COMPUTERNAME`, `PUBLIC`, `ALLUSERSPROFILE`.

This breaks standard toolchains inside agent sessions:

- `dotnet build` / `dotnet restore` fail on every project with `NuGet.targets(782,5): error : Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'path1')` — NuGet resolves its config path from `APPDATA`. Aspire's `Aspire.AppHost.Sdk` resolution fails the same way ("Failed to load NuGet settings. Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'path1')").
- `gh` (GitHub CLI) cannot find its keyring credentials/config (stored under `%AppData%\GitHub CLI`) and reports it is not authenticated, even though it is.

Exporting `APPDATA` etc. manually inside the shell command works around it, which the agent has to rediscover in every session.

## Root cause

`out/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostMain.js` builds the environment for the agent runtime spawn from scratch instead of inheriting `process.env`. Deminified:

```js
function buildEnv(clean = true) {
  let env = clean
    ? { ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE: "1",
        NODE_OPTIONS: undefined,
        ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: undefined,
        HOME: process.env.HOME,
        USERPROFILE: process.env.USERPROFILE,
        CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD: "1" }
    : { ...process.env, ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE: "1", NODE_OPTIONS: undefined };
  env["AI_AGENT"] = "github_copilot_vscode_agent";
  for (const k of Object.keys(process.env))
    if (k !== "ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE" && (k.startsWith("VSCODE_") || k.startsWith("ELECTRON_")))
      env[k] = undefined;
  return env;
}
```

The Claude session spawn takes the `clean = true` branch, so only `HOME` and `USERPROFILE` survive from the parent environment. Downstream, the SDK re-adds `PATH`, `TEMP`, `USERNAME`, etc., and the MSYS runtime (Git Bash) synthesizes `SYSTEMROOT`/`WINDIR` when missing (verified with `env -i bash -c env`) — but nothing restores `APPDATA` and the other variables listed above, so every child process of the agent's shell runs without them.

The env-hygiene intent (stripping `VSCODE_*`/`ELECTRON_*`, unsetting `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) is sound, but on Windows an allowlist of only `HOME`+`USERPROFILE` is too aggressive: `APPDATA`/`ProgramFiles`/`ComSpec`/`PATHEXT` are not secrets, they are part of the OS contract that virtually every Windows CLI depends on.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On Windows, open a repo in VS Code and start a Claude agent session from the Agents window.
2. Ask the agent to run `dotnet restore` on any solution (or simply `echo %APPDATA%` / `printenv APPDATA`).
3. `APPDATA` is empty and NuGet fails with `Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'path1')`. Running the same command in the integrated terminal works fine.

## Suggested fix

In the `clean` branch, preserve the standard Windows system/user-profile variables (e.g. `APPDATA`, `LOCALAPPDATA`, `ProgramData`, `ProgramFiles`, `ProgramFiles(x86)`, `CommonProgramFiles*`, `ComSpec`, `PATHEXT`, `SystemRoot`, `SystemDrive`, `windir`, `OS`, `NUMBER_OF_PROCESSORS`, `PROCESSOR_*`, `COMPUTERNAME`, `PUBLIC`, `ALLUSERSPROFILE`, `DriverData`) the same way `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` are preserved — or reuse the inherit branch plus an explicit denylist for secrets.

Related: #316791 (same class of problem — agent session environment missing `GIT_ASKPASS`).

title: Copilot AH should not access files in non-trusted folders
body:
When an Copilot SDK session's working directory is not inside a Git repository, customization discovery goes up the parent chain until the user's home directory to look for customization files. 
As a result, project-scoped customizations can be inherited from every ancestor between the working directory and $HOME, including $HOME itself.

That's useful for mono-repo use cases, but Copilot should check whether these folders are trusted.

I filed the following issues against the SDK:
https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/issues/13531
Also it seems that it even goes into sibling directories
https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/issues/16814

title: Fix New Chat Window crash by creating the parked chat pet host in the main window realm
body:
## Description

Opening **New Chat Window** failed immediately with `Not allowed to create elements in child window JavaScript context.`, leaving the chat editor unrendered.

`ChatPetWidgetCoordinator.createDormantHost` created the parked pet host through the *host's* owner document. In an auxiliary window that document's `createElement` is replaced with a throwing stub by `BrowserAuxiliaryWindowService.createContainer`, so the first pet-host registration in that window threw during `ChatWidget.render` → `EditorPane.createEditor`.

Regressed in 1cecb47 (#332153), which introduced the coordinator.

### Changes

- `createDormantHost()` builds its detached parent with `dom.$` — the main window realm, matching how `ChatPetWidget` creates the rest of its DOM. The host argument was only used for its owner document and is dropped.

```diff
-	private createDormantHost(host: IChatPetWidgetHost): IChatPetWidgetHost {
-		const parent = host.parent.ownerDocument.createElement('div');
+	private createDormantHost(): IChatPetWidgetHost {
+		// Auxiliary windows forbid `createElement` on their own document, so the
+		// parked host is created in the main window realm.
+		const parent = dom.$('div');
```

- Regression test registering a pet host owned by an auxiliary document whose `createElement` throws (the established iframe pattern used by `voiceGlow`/`chatClipboard` tests); it reproduces the reported stack without the fix. `createHost()` in the suite now accepts an optional parent.

The parked element is never attached, so only its owner document changes; host activation still re-parents the overlay into the real (auxiliary) host.

### Not addressed

`chatRichLink.ts` and `sessions/.../chatBackgroundRenderer.ts` have the same `ownerDocument.createElement` pattern and are separate latent issues; left out to keep this fix scoped.

body:
## Problem

Chat session management keybindings are inconsistent across chat surfaces:

- The existing session Rename command is available from the sessions UI, but its keybinding does not work when focus is in the panel/editor chat transcript or input.
- The Agents Window exposes Rename without an equivalent list/chat keybinding.
- The editor session list uses Delete to Archive (or Mark as Done), while the Agents Window does not provide the same keyboard behavior.
- Rename must follow the active session's actual capability. Unsupported contributed sessions (for example, cloud sessions) and provisional Agent Host sessions before their first request must not consume the keybinding or show an unsupported-renaming error.
- Session-list Archive must not steal editing keys from chat/find inputs, fall back to an unrelated active chat, or conflict with Delete Chat. Permanent Delete should remain an explicit context-menu action.

## Expected behavior

### Panel and editor chat

- Press F2 from either the current chat transcript or chat input to invoke Rename.
- Preserve the existing macOS Enter binding only while the session list is focused; Enter in the transcript or input must retain its normal activation/submit behavior.
- Resolve the session from the actually focused chat widget, rather than a stale item in the sessions viewer.
- Keep focused-chat F2 available even if the sessions viewer retains a stale multi-selection; the multi-selection guard applies only to list-based Rename.
- Local sessions support Rename.
- Contributed sessions support Rename only when their loaded session exposes the rename capability.
- Unsupported cloud sessions do not receive the Rename keybinding.
- A provisional Agent Host session does not receive Rename before its first request; after materialization, Rename is available when supported.

### Agents Window

- Press F2 to invoke Rename from the focused Sessions-list item or from the active session's chat transcript/input.
- Require actual Sessions-list focus for list-based Rename so focus in the view header or toolbar cannot rename an unrelated active session.
- Press Delete on Windows/Linux or Cmd+Backspace on macOS from the Sessions list to Archive or Mark as Done the focused non-archived selection, including multi-selection.
- Ignore sessions that are already archived, and do not fall back to an active chat when the Sessions list itself is not focused.
- Do not invoke Archive while a Sessions-list input (such as Find) is focused.
- Keep permanent Delete in the session context menu without a default keybinding.
- Keep Delete Chat scoped to the chat grid, and do not run destructive actions while a text input is focused.

### Accessibility

- Document the Rename and Archive/Mark as Done shortcuts in the existing chat accessibility help.
- Explain that permanent Delete remains in the context menu, Agent Host Rename becomes available after the first request, and Rename is capability-dependent.

## Validation steps

1. Open a local chat in the Chat panel. Focus the transcript, press F2, and verify the title prompt targets that chat. Repeat from the chat input.
2. Open a local chat editor and repeat the transcript/input F2 Rename checks. Verify F2 still works after multi-selecting sessions in the panel's session list and returning focus to chat.
3. On macOS, verify Enter still renames a focused session-list item but submits/activates normally in the chat input/transcript; F2 invokes Rename from chat.
4. Open a new Agent Host chat editor. Before sending a request, press F2 and verify no rename prompt or unsupported-renaming warning appears. Send the first request, then verify F2 works when the materialized session supports Rename.
5. Open a contributed session that does not support Rename (for example, a cloud session) and verify F2 is not active.
6. In the Agents Window, focus a renameable session in the Sessions list, press F2, and verify the focused session is targeted. Move focus to the view header/toolbar and verify F2 does not rename the active session.
7. In the Agents Window, focus the active session's transcript and input and verify F2 targets the active session when supported.
8. Select one or more non-archived sessions in the Sessions list, press Delete on Windows/Linux or Cmd+Backspace on macOS, and verify they are archived or marked done rather than permanently deleted.
9. Include an already archived session in the selection and verify it is ignored. Move focus outside the Sessions list and verify Archive does not fall back to the active chat.
10. Focus the Sessions-list Find input and verify Delete/Cmd+Backspace edits the input instead of archiving a session.
11. Open a session's context menu and verify Delete remains available as the explicit permanent-deletion action.
12. Focus a chat input and verify Delete/Cmd+Backspace remains an editing operation. Verify Delete Chat still works from its intended chat-grid context.
13. Open Chat Accessibility Help and verify the session Rename, Archive/Mark as Done, and permanent Delete guidance is present with dynamic keybinding labels.

## Automated validation

Validated after merging current `main` and resolving review feedback:

- Focused chat/session action and accessibility tests: 32 passed.
- Core Typecheck: 0 errors.
- All review threads resolved.

## Problem

Restoring several persisted multi-root Copilot CLI sessions can trigger enough concurrent Agent Host Git work that background branch-summary probes hit the hard 5-second timeout. Repositories whose probe times out are omitted from the all-folder changes summary.

This was observed in recent Code - Insiders 1.135.0-insider sessions with trace logging enabled. Exact timeout counts:

- `20260825T095440/agenthost.4.log`: 61 occurrences of `timed out after 5000ms`
- `20260825T161812/agenthost.3.log`: 5 occurrences

## Log excerpt

```text
2026-08-25 09:55:45.188 [warning] [agentHostGitService] > git for-each-ref --format=%(refname) refs/heads/main refs/remotes/origin/main failed: git for-each-ref timed out after 5000ms
2026-08-25 09:55:45.493 [warning] [agentHostGitService] > git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all failed: git status timed out after 5000ms
2026-08-25 09:55:45.493 [error] [AgentHostChangesetService] Git branch diff unavailable for multi-folder branch summary copilotcli:/d2150ccd-617b-41bc-ab2d-0536b1e8b2f3 in repository file:///Users/chrmarti/Development/repos/copilot-agent-runtime; skipping that repository.
2026-08-25 09:55:45.513 [warning] [agentHostGitService] > git rev-parse HEAD failed: git rev-parse timed out after 5000ms
2026-08-25 09:55:45.548 [warning] [agentHostGitService] > git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all failed: git status timed out after 5000ms
2026-08-25 09:55:45.548 [error] [AgentHostChangesetService] Git branch diff unavailable for multi-folder branch summary copilotcli:/d2150ccd-617b-41bc-ab2d-0536b1e8b2f3 in repository file:///Users/chrmarti/Development/repos/copilot-sdk; skipping that repository.
2026-08-25 09:55:45.603 [warning] [agentHostGitService] > git merge-base HEAD origin/main failed: git merge-base timed out after 5000ms
2026-08-25 09:55:45.732 [warning] [agentHostGitService] > git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all failed: git status timed out after 5000ms
2026-08-25 09:55:45.733 [error] [AgentHostChangesetService] Git branch diff unavailable for multi-folder branch summary copilotcli:/d2150ccd-617b-41bc-ab2d-0536b1e8b2f3 in repository file:///Users/chrmarti/Development/repos/mxc; skipping that repository.
```

A second startup showed the same sequence:

```text
2026-08-25 16:19:06.843 [trace] [SessionDataService] Opening database: /Users/chrmarti/Library/Application Support/Code - Insiders/agentSessionData/d9e040fb-1f24-4d82-9bdf-eac810b2f491/session.db
2026-08-25 16:19:06.845 [warning] [agentHostGitService] > git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all failed: git status timed out after 5000ms
2026-08-25 16:19:06.845 [error] [AgentHostChangesetService] Git branch diff unavailable for multi-folder branch summary copilotcli:/dc5a92c4-1011-4135-a005-f9ed33fb0304 in repository file:///Users/chrmarti/Development/repos/kusto-script; skipping that repository.
```

## Analysis

The concurrency limit introduced with #329531 appears to be local to one summary computation:

- `_updateMultiFolderChangesSummary` constructs a new `Limiter(5)` for each invocation.
- Static recomputes are sequenced by session and changeset kind, so computations for different restored sessions can run concurrently.
- Each repository diff is itself a pipeline of several Git commands.
- The primary repository diff is computed separately from the multi-root summary limiter.

This means the effective process-wide concurrency can be much greater than five when several multi-root sessions restore together. The logs show many session databases opening and Git pipelines running in the same short interval, followed by timeout clusters.

This is a hypothesis, not a proposed fix. Repository size, disk contention, and the 5-second timeout may also contribute. It would be useful to determine whether static multi-root summary work should:

1. share a process/service-wide concurrency budget,
2. be deferred until its summary is requested, or
3. use a different timeout policy for background summary computation.

## Impact

- Multi-root session change counts can be incomplete because timed-out repositories are skipped.
- Startup/restoration produces repeated Agent Host warnings and errors.
- Concurrent Git processes add avoidable startup I/O and CPU pressure.

Related implementation: #329531

title: SSH connection establishing issue, only on windows.
body: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No - VS Code Version: 1.134.0 - OS Version: Microsoft Windows [Version 10.0.26200.9168] Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open VS Code on a Windows machine. 2. Use the Remote - SSH extension to connect to any SSH host. 3. Attempt to establish the SSH connection. Actual Result: VS Code fails to establish the connection and shows the following error: Could not establish connection to "72.62.2x9.xxx": Extension 'ms-vscode-remote.remote-ssh' CANNOT use API proposal: terminalRemoteResolver. Its package.json#enabledApiProposals-property declares: resolvers, tunnels, terminalDataWriteEvent, contribRemoteHelp, contribViewsRemote, telemetry but NOT terminalRemoteResolver. The missing proposal MUST be added and you must start in extension development mode or use the following command line switch: --enable-proposed-api ms-vscode-remote.remote-ssh. Expected Result: VS Code should establish the SSH connection successfully. Additional Information: This issue started occurring today on my Windows machine without any intentional changes to the SSH configuration. The same SSH host can be accessed successfully: - Using Cursor IDE on the same Windows machine. - Using VS Code from a Linux machine. This suggests that the issue is specific to VS Code on the Windows machine rather than the SSH server or its configuration. I have attached a screenshot showing the error.

title: Refine nested chat interactions in the Sessions list
body: ## Summary - Show user-facing chats as selectable child rows beneath their parent session. - Add token-based hierarchy connectors that appear only while the expanded chat family is hovered, focused, or selected. - Route the parent row consistently to the main chat while preserving exact child selection, side-open, drag, and keyboard behavior. - Cover connector visibility, selection persistence, collapse/expand, routing, and native twistie behavior with focused tests. ## Why Nested chats need enough structure to be scannable without adding persistent visual noise to every session. Interaction-aware connectors communicate the active hierarchy, native child selection keeps keyboard and pointer behavior consistent with the tree, and treating the parent as the main-chat entry point makes navigation predictable. Row-owned connector segments also work with virtualized clipping, while existing color, spacing, stroke, and radius tokens keep the treatment aligned with the workbench. ## Screenshots and video https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fae45702-4da3-4063-ad40-a6677204a78b ## Testing - `npm run transpile-client` - `./scripts/test.sh --runInBand --grep "Sessions - SessionsList"` (53 passing) - Targeted ESLint for the changed TypeScript files - Targeted Stylelint for `sessionsList.css` - Editor diagnostics and `git diff --check`
